image.missing.note: Most platforms show a thumbnail with each headline. A platform that skips articles without one says so in its own pack.

image.too_small.note: The smallest featured image News Distribution accepts without a tip is 640 by 360 px. A platform that asks for more says so in its own pack.

image.bad_ratio.note: A featured image between square and 2.5 times as wide as it is tall crops well in most thumbnails. A platform that asks for a different shape says so in its own pack.

image.alt_missing.note: Alt text describes the image for people who cannot see it. It is the text a platform or a screen reader falls back on.

credit.missing.note: A credit says who made the image. The Image credits settings decide whether one is required and what happens when it is missing.

title.long.note: A limit of 110 characters set by News Distribution. Platforms that state their own limit say so in their packs.

title.short.note: A limit of 10 characters set by News Distribution. A very short title says little in a feed.

title.publication_name.note: Titles read better in a feed without the publication name. A platform that asks for this says so in its own pack.

title.author.note: Titles read better in a feed without the author name. A platform that asks for this says so in its own pack.

title.date.note: Titles read better in a feed without the date. News Distribution looks for a written date such as 21/10/2026 or 2026-10-21, so it can miss a date written in words.

date.invalid.note: A published article needs a publication date after 1990.

date.future.note: A publication date in the future is not a date a platform can accept yet.

date.modified_before_published.note: A modified date earlier than the publication date contradicts itself.

body.empty.note: An article with no text and no media has nothing to send.

body.short.note: A limit of 50 words set by News Distribution. Platforms that state their own minimum say so in their packs.

body.shortcode_left_as_text.note: A shortcode that no active plugin handles prints as plain text in a feed. News Distribution reads the saved text only and cannot run a shortcode to see its result.

body.broken_markup.note: Unclosed or stray tags can cut a feed entry short or break it.

duplicate.title.note: Two articles in one language with the same title look like a duplicate to a platform.

clash.title.note: The same title in two languages often means a translation was copied without being translated.

clash.address.note: Two articles on one web address leave a platform with one page for both.

byline.missing.note: Many platforms ask for an author on each article.

byline.not_a_person.note: An account such as admin is not a person. The Authors settings say what is sent instead.

republished.address_missing.note: A copy that points to its source needs the source's address. Without it the copy is kept out of search instead, so it is never sent out unprotected.

republished.no_source.note: A line at the end of a republished article says where it came from. Without a source name no line is added.

republished.duplicate_risk.note: A copy of another source's article that is still sent to a partner feed or an outlet may be treated as a duplicate of the original. Whether a platform does is its own decision.

video.upload_date_missing.note: Google asks for an upload date for a video. News Distribution never uses the article's date in its place, because that would tell search the video is newer than it is.

video.name_missing.note: Google asks for a name for a video. A video with no name gets no video markup.

video.thumbnail_missing.note: Google asks for a thumbnail for a video. A video with none gets no video markup.

video.unavailable.note: A video that its site says is private or removed gets no video markup. This is known only when the lookup of video details is on.
